title: Credit in Sonpur
body: Two students visited Sonpur, a small irrigated village where potato is grown. Shyamal, a small farmer with 1.5 acres, earlier borrowed from the village moneylender at 5 per cent per month. Now he borrows from an agricultural trader at 3 per cent per month; the trader supplies farm inputs on credit and makes farmers promise to sell their crop to him at harvest, when prices are low. Arun, who owns seven acres, is one of the few people in Sonpur with a bank loan for cultivation, at 8.5 per cent per annum, repayable any time in three years. He plans to sell part of his crop, store the rest in cold storage and take a fresh bank loan against the cold storage receipt. Rama, a landless agricultural labourer, has no work for several months a year. She borrows from her employer, a medium landowner, at 5 per cent per month and repays by working for him. She often takes a fresh loan before the previous one is repaid and now owes Rs 5,000.
